title: Night begins at Paranal Observatory
caption: Nightfall at the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Three large telescope enclosures stand in the foreground as night falls, with a crescent Moon shining on the right. A soft glow rises from the lower right toward the Moon, while the Milky Way climbs from the lower left to the top of the frame. These are three of the four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope, photographed looking west, with Yepun (UT4) closest to the camera.
The rising glow is zodiacal light, which is sunlight bouncing off dust that drifts between the planets in the plane of the ecliptic, the path the Sun appears to follow across the sky.

Near the top of the picture, part of the central bulge of our galaxy shows through. The dark lanes along the Milky Way are enormous clouds of interstellar dust that soak up visible light and give the energy back out at longer wavelengths.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph of the Very Large Telescope taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye, so the faint zodiacal light and the dust lanes of the Milky Way are easier to see here than they would be in person.

explore: Just to the upper left of Yepun, the caption points out the Southern Cross and a dark nebula known as the Coal Sack, a patch of dust that blocks the starlight behind it.
alt: Three telescope enclosures at nightfall, a crescent Moon on the right, a glow rising toward it, and the Milky Way stretching from lower left to the top.
